Title: Bringing GPT-Rosalind to academic research labs

URL Source: https://openai.com/index/introducing-the-rosalind-academic-plan

Markdown Content:
We’re introducing the Rosalind Academic Plan to help more academic scientists access [GPT‑Rosalind⁠](https://openai.com/rosalind/), our dedicated life sciences model, which combines frontier reasoning with [Rosalind workbench⁠(opens in a new window)](https://developers.openai.com/blog/rosalind-workbench) that enables specialized tool orchestration across medicinal chemistry, genomics, wet-lab assistance, and other scientific applications. Eligible labs can receive up to 30 Business Standard seats at no cost for up to 12 months, with access to GPT‑Rosalind subject to trusted-access approval.

Academic research creates knowledge that entire fields build on. Work that begins with a fundamental question about biology can eventually change how we diagnose disease, develop medicines, or grow food. But those advances depend on scientists having the resources to explore ideas, test them, and share what they learn.

Accelerating scientific discovery is central to OpenAI’s mission of ensuring that artificial general intelligence benefits all of humanity. With this plan, we’re investing in the scientists doing that foundational work—helping more labs combine their expertise and judgment with AI tools built for life sciences research.

## Supporting the research behind future breakthroughs

Many of the advances we rely on today grew out of years of basic research.

The Human Genome Project helped launch modern genomics, transforming medicine, diagnostics, and biotechnology.

Curiosity-driven work on bacterial immune systems led to CRISPR-Cas9, which revolutionized genome editing and is now advancing research in cancer, inherited disease, agriculture, and biotechnology. Decades of university research on mRNA also laid the groundwork for COVID-19 vaccines and a new generation of vaccines and therapies.

Academic research has always laid the groundwork for advances in medicine and biotechnology. By helping more scientists combine their scientific expertise and judgment with the advanced specialized reasoning of GPT‑Rosalind, we hope to support discoveries whose benefits reach far beyond the lab.

## How academic labs are using GPT‑Rosalind

OpenAI is committed to enabling academic researchers to pursue their scientific ambitions. Distinguished academic labs are already exploring how GPT‑Rosalind can support work ranging from protein design to understanding neurodegeneration. These examples show where researchers are applying the model within their scientific workflows.

1 of 3

## What the plan includes

With the new Rosalind Academic Plan, academic researchers can bring GPT‑Rosalind and Rosalind Workbench to their lab with greater flexibility and harness frontier model intelligence for scientific research.

Eligible labs receive:

*   Up to 30 Business Standard seats at $0 per user per month for up to 12 months.

*   Access to all commercially available frontier OpenAI models, subject to plan usage limits.

*   Access to GPT‑Rosalind following trusted-access approval.

Research data shared through the Rosalind Academic Plan is not used to train our models by default.

## Build for life sciences research

GPT‑Rosalind is a specialized life sciences model designed to support deeper reasoning on complex biological questions. Through trusted access, approved researchers can use it to investigate sensitive scientific questions within safeguards designed for legitimate research.

Areas of research include:

### Drug and protein design

Designing candidate drugs, therapeutic proteins, peptides, and enzymes, and optimizing their molecular interactions, selectivity, stability, and suitability for development.

Card 1 of 7: Drug and protein design

## Apply on behalf of your lab

The Rosalind Academic Plan is currently available to academic labs at U.S. universities. PIs and lab leads at universities without an OpenAI Enterprise agreement can apply on behalf of their labs through our trusted access process. Labs at universities with an existing agreement must apply through their university’s Enterprise access process.

Once approved, PIs and lab leads can activate free access to GPT‑Rosalind for up to 30 named members, alongside the other OpenAI frontier models included in the plan. API access is not included at this time. Verified PIs and lab leads manage member permissions and are responsible for their lab’s approved use.

### Get started with GPT‑Rosalind

Choose the application path for your lab or organization.

GPT‑Rosalind access is subject to approval.

Learn more about eligibility, application requirements, and getting started in our [**help center guide**⁠(opens in a new window)](https://help.openai.com/articles/20001602).

## Responsible access for scientific research

Before activating access, we:

*   Verify the institution’s legitimacy and the PI or lab lead’s identity

*   Review the lead’s professional background, institutional appointment, and authority to oversee lab access

*   Assess the lab’s institutional affiliation, research activities, and intended use

*   Establish clear responsibilities for the lab lead and a designated institutional safety contact

Safeguards continue after activation through monitoring and enforcement. For registered high-sensitivity use cases, our safety checks account for the approved research context. When questions arise, we may follow up with researchers to clarify the work and confirm authorization. This approach is designed to detect potential misuse while accounting for legitimate research context and reducing unnecessary interruptions to authorized work.

## Specialized intelligence for complex scientific questions

## Get started

We’re starting with academic labs as part of a broader effort to put useful AI tools in the hands of more scientists. By lowering the cost of access, we hope to give more researchers room to pursue ideas whose benefits could reach far beyond their own labs—from a clearer understanding of disease to better treatments and more resilient food systems.

Those advances will come from scientists asking important questions and doing the work to answer them. We want to help more of them do that work.

If you’re affiliated with an academic lab, learn more about the Rosalind Academic Plan and [check whether you’re eligible⁠(opens in a new window)](https://chatgpt.com/rosalind/lab/application).

Title: Teaching students to think and learn through questions

URL Source: https://openai.com/index/teaching-students-to-think-and-learn-through-questions

Markdown Content:
On Teachers’ Day, we celebrate those who help us learn. A good question can change the course of a lesson. It can bring an unspoken question to light, open up another way to solve a problem, or help someone recognize what they already know. Teachers do this work every day: they know their students, choose how to introduce an idea, and guide them from their first attempt to understanding.

Set in a university classroom, the campaign takes a humorous look at the changing relationship between teachers and students and celebrates the role of educators in a world with AI.

## AI for Educators now available in Portuguese

Today, we are launching the [**AI for Educators**⁠(opens in a new window)](https://academy.openai.com/home/courses/ai-for-educators-lc8j1) course in Brazilian Portuguese on OpenAI Academy, OpenAI’s free learning platform. Designed for educators in primary, secondary, and higher education, the course shows how to use AI to plan lessons, create activities and assessments, and prepare communications while preserving educators’ pedagogical judgment.

## Learning through active participation, step by step

[Study Mode helps you explore a subject⁠(opens in a new window)](https://chatgpt.com/features/study-mode/) step by step, with questions, hints, explanations, and checks for understanding. Developed in collaboration with teachers, scientists, and experts in pedagogy, the feature aims to encourage active participation and reflection on one’s own reasoning.

To turn on **Study Mode**, select Study from the tools menu in ChatGPT.

A student reviewing biology, for example, might ask: “I’m studying enzymes. Ask me one question at a time, wait for my answer, and help me identify what I need to review.”

Teachers can also try Study Mode with subjects they know well, looking at whether the questions encourage reasoning and whether the explanations are appropriate for their class.

In a science lesson on evaporation, for example, a teacher might ask students to investigate why clothes dry on a clothesline. After exploring the topic with Study Mode, each student writes their own explanation and a question to discuss in class, without referring back to the conversation. The teacher can use these responses to identify what needs to be revisited with the class.

This Teachers’ Day, we invite you to experiment: explore the AI for Educators course, try Study Mode, and discover how these tools can be useful in different teaching contexts. Technology can open up new ways to learn, but it is teachers who know their students, ask the most important questions, and help turn curiosity into knowledge.

# Be There for the Beginning: Celebrate the Launch of NVIDIA RTX Spark

 Explore a new era of local AI, join launch celebrations around the world and #ShareYourSpark.

October 15, 2026 by[Shreevar Rastogi](https://blogs.nvidia.com/blog/author/shreevarr/ "Posts by Shreevar Rastogi")

 Share

Share This Article

A new beginning for Windows PCs starts tomorrow with the launch of [NVIDIA RTX Spark](https://www.nvidia.com/en-us/products/rtx-spark/) — one PC built for creators, gamers and AI agents. All are invited to celebrate with NVIDIA and partners at launch events around the world.

## **Share Your Spark**

Every PC has a story. What was your first Windows PC, and what did it spark a love for? Join the celebration online by sharing responses with **#ShareYourSpark** for a chance to win an ASUS ProArt P14 RTX Spark laptop signed by NVIDIA founder and CEO Jensen Huang. [See the campaign and official rules](https://www.nvidia.com/en-us/products/rtx-spark/share-your-spark-sweepstakes/).

## **See What Reviewers Are Saying**

From local AI workflows to creative apps and gaming, see what reviewers are saying about RTX Spark — then experience it at a launch celebration.

_“The fact that NVIDIA, Microsoft and their partners have delivered such a capable, compatible and polished platform even in its first at-bat should put the rest of the PC industry on notice.” — [Tom’s Hardware](https://www.tomshardware.com/laptops/we-test-the-rtx-spark-superchip-in-microsofts-surface-laptop-ultra-nvidias-windows-on-arm-platform-impresses-in-local-ai-but-gaming-isnt-its-strong-suit)_

_“I tested NVIDIA’s RTX Spark for gaming and local AI – the performance absolutely stunned me.” — [TrustedReviews](https://www.trustedreviews.com/opinion/nvidia-rtx-spark-for-gaming-and-local-ai-testing-benchmarks-performance), UK_

_“I’m very happy to report that performance is actually looking really good when it comes to AI, gaming and creative workflows.” — [Microcenter](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=Rqtdx4V0TkQ)_

_“[RTX Spark] is a different species of computer that has arrived early. It is a statement of intent from NVIDIA about where computing is going — trading raw benchmarking crowns for the ability to carry a self-rewriting, fully autonomous, CUDA-accelerated digital brain in your backpack.” —[Tom’s Guide](https://www.tomsguide.com/computing/cpus/ive-been-living-with-nvidias-rtx-spark-for-a-week-on-surface-laptop-ultra-its-not-a-macbook-pro-killer-but-something-much-weirder-and-wildly-powerful)_

_“One of the most impressive parts of the launch is how many apps NVIDIA has worked with to ensure optimisation with the Spark technology.” —[Creative Bloq](https://www.creativebloq.com/features/nvidia-rtx-spark-all-you-need-to-know-as-a-creative)_

Independent testing from Artificial Analysis offers an early look at the powerful local AI performance RTX Spark brings to a laptop.

## **Join the Launch Celebrations**

On Friday, Oct. 16, get hands on with RTX Spark at launch events around the world. Explore demos for creating, developing and gaming, connect with fellow enthusiasts and discover what local AI can do.

Times below are local. Follow each event’s entry instructions. Space is limited.

*   **San Francisco** — Best Buy, 1717 Harrison Street, 10 a.m.-12 p.m. Try hands-on demos, meet iJustine and hear fireside conversations with local tech founders. Free, first-come, first-served entry; no ticket required. [Event details](https://luma.com/rtx-spark-launch-celebration-SF).
*   **Berlin** — Xperion at Saturn, Alexanderplatz 3, 7-10:30 p.m. Explore hands-on demos and stage programming with creators and developers. Registration required. [RSVP](https://luma.com/rtx-spark-launch-celebration).
*   **Taipei** — Muse Garden, No. 88 Yanchang Road. Join an evening of demos, music and AI community discussions, with shopping and networking continuing until 10:15 p.m. [Registration required](https://events.nvidia.com/rtx-spark-taipei).
*   **Beijing** — JD MALL Beijing Shuangjing Store, No. 31 Guangqu Road. Check in begins at 7 p.m. Launch celebration starts at 8 p.m., followed by hands-on demos. Event concludes at 9:30 p.m. Register through WeChat.
*   **Istanbul** — Vatan Bilgisayar Topkapı, Mevlana Caddesi No. 138. Explore hands-on demos and local creator programming. Walk-in entry; no advance registration required.
*   **Seoul** — COEX East Lobby, 513 Yeongdong-daero. Hands-on demos begin at 7 p.m., with gaming and AI creator programming from 8 p.m. Event concludes at 9:30 p.m. No advance registration required.

Title: Open From Data Center to Desktop: NVIDIA Expands Nemotron Family With Highest Efficiency Super VL and Bolt Models

URL Source: https://blogs.nvidia.com/blog/nemotron-3-5-super-vl/

Published Time: 2026-10-15T15:00:24+00:00

Markdown Content:
NVIDIA today released Nemotron 3.5 Super VL, an open 120-billion-parameter model that delivers the fastest task completion and highest accuracy for specialized always-on agents.

Joining it are two new edge models: Nemotron 3.5 Bolt 74B-A9B 24GB, optimized to balance intelligence and speed per GB for local agentic workloads, and Nemotron 3.5 Bolt E4B 4GB, optimized for intelligence per GB for fast conversational agents.

Super VL and Bolt 74B-A9B are available now, with Bolt E4B coming Oct. 23.****The three [open models](https://www.nvidia.com/en-us/glossary/open-models/) together cover the full range of agent deployments, from large enterprise servers down to edge devices and local hardware.

Any organization that wants to run agents on NVIDIA infrastructure now has an open, optimized model for their tier, without having to choose between capability and deployability.

Super VL and Bolt join the Nemotron family alongside [Lightning](https://blogs.nvidia.com/blog/nemotron-lightning-switchyard-rtx-dgx/) and Ultra.

Lightning, released in August, handles high-throughput workloads; Ultra handles the hardest reasoning tasks; and Bolt brings intelligence to the edge.

## **Nemotron 3.5 Super VL: Frontier Accuracy at One-Fifth the Size**

Super VL, built in collaboration with the [Nemotron Coalition](https://nvidianews.nvidia.com/news/nvidia-launches-nemotron-coalition-of-leading-global-ai-labs-to-advance-open-frontier-models), delivers leading accuracy on multimodal agentic tasks — instruction following, tool use, multistep business workflows, and visual understanding — comparable with NVIDIA’s largest reasoning model at roughly one-fifth the parameter count.

Nemotron 3.5 Super VL delivers frontier-level intelligence in its class for high-volume agentic workflows.

As the fastest open agentic model in its class — 5x faster than the next best — it helps enterprise agents complete high-volume tasks faster across workflows that span days or weeks.

Nemotron 3.5 Super VL, on Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index leadboard, achieves up to 5x faster throughput compared to other models in its class.

Unlike closed frontier models, organizations can post-train Super VL on their own data, deploy it on their own infrastructure and oversee what they build.

## Nemotron 3.5 Bolt: Agentic Intelligence at the Edge

Bolt 74B-A9B 24GB is designed to run everyday agentic tasks locally on NVIDIA RTX/DGX Spark, using a native 2-bit quantization to fit in 24GB of memory and run alongside other applications.

Relative to other models with a similar memory footprint, it provides a good balance of intelligence and speed: smart enough to get most jobs done, yet much faster than the smartest models.

With Bolt 74B-A9B 24GB, users can delegate their projects to popular local agent harnesses — from researching the web to writing to debugging code — all without sending those workloads to the cloud. It is the #1 open model in its class on [PinchBench](https://pinchbench.com/?slm=true), and the #2 open model for [BrowseComp](https://leaderboard.steel.dev/leaderboards/browsecomp/?weights=open&sizes=tiny%2Csmall%2Cmedium).

Bolt E4B 4GB is built for physical and conversational agents on GeForce RTX, Jetson, and RTX/DGX Spark. It combines natural conversation with multi-turn agentic capabilities to power fast local voice assistants, interactive characters and embedded interfaces.

## **Adoption of Custom Super Intelligence**

Dozens of organizations across industries are post-training Super VL on their own data, tools, policies and workflows to push accuracy higher on the specialized tasks that define their agent deployments.

Super VL is being post-trained and customized by organizations across industries. [Scale AI](https://scale.com/blog/scale-partners-with-nvidia) post-trained the model for Skydance’s vendor credit finance agent and for EY’s M&A due diligence agent.AfterQuery customized the model for Hebbia for credit agreement analysis. [AI21](https://www.ai21.com/blog/ai21-post-trains-nvidia-nemotron-35-super-vl/) and [Alice](http://alice.io/blog/nemotron-ai21) post-trained the model for cybersecurity attack resilience.Mercor post-trained the model on APEX-SWE coding benchmark, for coding agents that plan, write and debug code. [ModelScope](https://modelscope.ai/collections/nv-community/Nemotron-35-Super-VL) enables developers to fine-tune the model through its [ms-swift](https://github.com/modelscope/ms-swift)framework for specialized multimodal applications.

Additional organizations customizing Nemotron 3.5 Super VL include Ramp for financial document intelligence; Dream, sovereign AI-powered cybersecurity research and vulnerability analysis; Lila Sciences for scientific discovery and search, and[R1](http://www.r1rcm.com/resources/long-context-medical-reasoning-to-reduce-denials-post-training-nvidia-nemotron-3-5-super)for medical claims analysis and revenue cycle management. TrainLoop post-trained the model with dermatology data from Nolla, which just became the first company approved for AI to write initial patient prescriptions.

Software platform companies integrating Nemotron 3.5 Super VL include:

*   **Atlassian****,**for tasks like agentic search across apps such as Jira and Confluence.
*   **CrowdStrike**, which is customizing the model for agentic blue teaming in enterprise security.
*   **Dassault Systèmes**, powering engineering design and simulation.
*   **Perplexity**, for search and agentic tasks in Perplexity Search and Computer.
*   **[Salesforce](https://www.salesforce.com/news/press-releases/2026/09/15/koa-reasoning-model/)**, which is customizing Nemotron to power AI agents that digitize and automate complex government workflows in secure customer environments through Missionforce Operations.
*   **Synopsys** software for semiconductor design verification interoperates with the model.

## What Nemotron 3.5 Super VL Actually Sees

Nemotron 3.5 Super VL’s [vision language](https://www.nvidia.com/en-us/glossary/vision-language-models/) strengths are targeted at what agents encounter in practice: optical character recognition, tables, charts and structured information in visual documents.

It processes a web page, extracts text, reads graphs and charts, and returns insights from what it finds. The same applies to PDFs and other documents agents commonly work with.

Nemotron 3.5 Super VL understands images, webpages and PDFs and acts on that understanding. Combining text and visual understanding in one model means agents don’t need to route tasks between separate systems — context carries through as work moves from document to data to decision.

## **Open for Maximum Control, Security, and Privacy**

Openness and customizability reinforce each other. The model ships with open weights, open datasets and training recipes.

Control runs in two directions. Organizations can run the model wherever their security and data-residency requirements dictate. They also choose to adopt a model they can adapt, rather than one subject to a provider’s restrictions.

In insurance, for example, a customized agent can scan claims for fraud markers on repeat. In financial services, an agent can review credit scores and flag activity against an organization’s own lending criteria. The model stays on premises. The data stays private.

Customization is supported through NVIDIA NeMo, Python-based pipelines and open datasets.

Nemotron 3.5 Super VL was trained on about 26 trillion tokens across [pretraining](https://huggingface.co/collections/nvidia/nemotron-pre-training-datasets) and continued pretraining, then post-trained with roughly 3.8 million samples and reinforcement learning across dozens of environments.

NVIDIA is also releasing open datasets on Hugging Face spanning [agentic tool use](https://huggingface.co/collections/nvidia/nemotron-post-training-v3), finance, instruction following, long context, fairness and vision-language understanding, along with the reinforcement learning environments in NeMo Gym.

[NVIDIA NIM](https://www.nvidia.com/en-us/ai-data-science/products/nim-microservices/) packages the model as a production-ready microservice with performance-optimized, validated configurations and enterprise-grade support, refreshed every two weeks with security patches and performance improvements.

And with the model running on NVIDIA Dynamo, organizations can serve up to 8x more users with 85% lower latency.

Nemotron 3.5 Super VL is available now on Hugging Face, Open Router, [ModelScope community](https://modelscope.ai/collections/nv-community/Nemotron-35-Super-VL) and as NVIDIA NIM.

## **Runs on DGX Spark, DGX Station, and RTX**

Nemotron 3.5 Super VL runs across NVIDIA’s full hardware stack: on [DGX Spark](https://www.nvidia.com/en-us/products/workstations/dgx-spark/), [DGX Station](https://www.nvidia.com/en-us/products/workstations/dgx-station/), RTX PRO and RTX systems for local intelligence at the desktop, on [NVIDIA Jetson](https://www.nvidia.com/en-us/autonomous-machines/embedded-systems/) at the edge, and across data center and cloud environments.

[Nemotron 3.5 Bolt 74B-A9B 24G B](https://research.nvidia.com/labs/nemotron/Nemotron-3.5-Bolt-24GB/) is available now on Hugging Face, with support for llama.cpp, [Ollama](https://huggingface.co/nvidia/NVIDIA-Nemotron-3.5-Bolt-74B-A9B-24GB-GGUF), [LM Studio](https://lmstudio.ai/models/nvidia/nemotron-3.5-bolt-74b-a9b), [Unsloth](https://unsloth.ai/docs/models/nemotron-3.5-bolt), and [vLLM](https://huggingface.co/nvidia/NVIDIA-Nemotron-3.5-Bolt-74B-A9B-24GB). Built for [NVIDIA RTX Spark laptops](https://www.nvidia.com/en-us/products/rtx-spark/) arriving Oct. 16, it also runs on [GeForce RTX PCs](https://www.nvidia.com/en-us/ai-on-rtx/), [DGX Spark](https://www.nvidia.com/en-us/products/workstations/dgx-spark/), [DGX Station](https://www.nvidia.com/en-us/products/workstations/dgx-station/) and [RTX PRO workstations](https://www.nvidia.com/en-us/products/workstations/).

Title: Dial Up the Cloud: NVIDIA DLSS 4.5 Controls Arrive on GeForce NOW

URL Source: https://blogs.nvidia.com/blog/geforce-now-thursday-enshrouded-update/

Published Time: 2026-10-15T13:00:59+00:00

Markdown Content:
Dial in the next gaming session this GFN Thursday. New NVIDIA DLSS 4.5 controls give [GeForce NOW](https://www.nvidia.com/en-us/geforce-now/)[members](https://www.nvidia.com/en-us/geforce-now/premium-memberships/) more choice over how supported games look and perform in the cloud, even without the latest hardware.

Then, step into the Shroud as Keen Games’ _Enshrouded_ leaves early access with its 1.0 release, or let the bolts fly in _Warhammer 40,000: Boltgun 2_. Both are streaming on GeForce NOW at launch.

With 10 new games joining the cloud this week, members can put the new controls to work in supported titles and keep playing across [supported devices](https://www.nvidia.com/en-us/geforce-now/system-reqs/) without downloads, installs or expensive hardware upgrades.

## **Fine-Tune the Cloud With DLSS 4.5 Controls**

More control, more cloud power.

NVIDIA [DLSS 4.5](https://www.nvidia.com/en-us/geforce/news/dlss-4-5-dynamic-multi-frame-gen-6x-2nd-gen-transformer-super-res/) controls are now available on GeForce NOW, giving members more choice over how supported games look and perform in the cloud, even without the latest hardware. DLSS Super Resolution sharpens image quality, while Dynamic Multi Frame Generation delivers lower latency and reduces stutter for smoother streaming, and Ray Reconstruction enhances ray-traced visuals. In addition, Ultimate members streaming on GeForce RTX 5080-powered cloud rigs benefit from the maximum available options, including Dynamic Multi Frame Generation up to 4X.

From James Bond’s globe-trotting missions in _007 First Light_ — now with [path tracing](https://blogs.nvidia.com/blog/geforce-now-thursday-aniimo/) support — to _CONTROL Resonant_’s reality-bending Manhattan and the shadowy scares of _Resident Evil Requiem_, the controls help fine-tune supported games for image quality, responsiveness or a preferred balance between the two.

These new settings are available in the GeForce NOW app under settings, for Windows, macOS, Chrome OS and Steam OS platforms. Members can read [here](https://nvidia.custhelp.com/app/answers/detail/a_id/5876) for more details on using the feature with their membership tier, and more information on how to get the smoothest cloud game streaming for some games on GeForce NOW.

## **Rise, Flameborn**

_Enshrouded_ 1.0 brings the co-op survival action role-playing game out of early access and into its full release. Rise as a Flameborn, the last ember of hope of a dying race, and venture into a vast world of survival, action and role-playing, where a corrupting fog has consumed a once-beautiful kingdom.

The title brings [improvements](https://enshrouded.com/en-US/news/were-still-cooking-for-10-heres-some-news-you-may-have-missed) to existing systems, alongside expansions [in combat](https://enshrouded.com/en-US/news/10-combat-changes-and-additions) with nine new spells, new mage and archer skills, reworked wands and upgradeable Eternal spells and arrows. New enemy variants keep encounters fresh, while a new biome raises the player level cap to 50 and equipment cap to 55.

GeForce NOW offers _Enshrouded_ 1.0 ready to play in the cloud at launch across supported devices. Skip the 60GB local install to save precious storage space, then step into the Shroud without waiting for downloads or needing to make room for the update.

## **Let the Bolts Fly**

_Warhammer 40,000: Boltgun 2_ is now streaming on GeForce NOW. The brutal, fast-paced sequel to the retro first-person shooter brings more enemies, more weapons and new ways to purge.

Picking up directly after the original game, a branching single-player campaign sends the fight to grimdark new worlds.

Choose between the formidable Sternguard Veteran Malum Caedo and the swift Sister of Battle Nyra Veyrath, each with distinct abilities, weapons and play styles. From towering hive cities to jungle mangrove swamps, new enemy types await in every biome.

GeForce NOW keeps the campaign ready in the cloud. No local rig upgrades or game installs stand between members and the fight — the Emperor’s work waits for no loading bar.

In addition, members can look for the following joining the [GeForce NOW library](https://www.nvidia.com/en-us/geforce-now/games/):

*   _Deep Dish Dungeon_ (New release on [Steam](https://store.steampowered.com/app/2871520?utm_source=nvidia&utm_campaign=geforce_now), Oct. 13)
*   _Planet Zoo 2_ (New release on [Steam](https://store.steampowered.com/app/3219030?utm_source=nvidia&utm_campaign=geforce_now), Oct. 13)
*   _Total War: SHOGUN 2 – Complete Edition_ (New release on [Steam](https://store.steampowered.com/app/3846830?utm_source=nvidia&utm_campaign=geforce_now), Oct. 13)
*   _Valor Mortis_ (New release on [Steam](https://store.steampowered.com/app/2828710?utm_source=nvidia&utm_campaign=geforce_now), Oct. 13)
*   _Among the Trolls_ (New release on [Steam](https://store.steampowered.com/app/1675260?utm_source=nvidia&utm_campaign=geforce_now), Oct. 14)
*   _over the hill_ (New release on [Steam](https://store.steampowered.com/app/2929250?utm_source=nvidia&utm_campaign=geforce_now), Oct. 14)
*   _Warhammer 40,000: Boltgun 2_ (New release on [Steam](https://store.steampowered.com/app/3115160?utm_source=nvidia&utm_campaign=geforce_now), Oct. 14)
*   _Beyond These Stars_ (New release on [Steam](https://store.steampowered.com/app/2295060?utm_source=nvidia&utm_campaign=geforce_now) and [Xbox](https://www.xbox.com/games/store/beyond-these-stars/9n4zmkc3gx4m?utm_source=nvidia&utm_campaign=geforce_now), Oct. 15), available on Game Pass
*   _Tenebris Somnia_ (New release on [Steam](https://store.steampowered.com/app/2121510?utm_source=nvidia&utm_campaign=geforce_now), Oct. 16)
*   _The Witcher 3: Wild Hunt – Remastered_ ([Xbox](https://www.xbox.com/games/store/the-witcher-3-wild-hunt-remastered/c261457lcnmj?utm_source=nvidia&utm_campaign=geforce_now)), available on Microsoft Store

Also this week, the performance of DLSS 5’s 3D-Guided Neural Rendering model is improving by 2X, enabling even more gamers to enjoy DLSS 5’s transformative uplift in lighting and materials at high frame rates and settings. The new, more performant [DLSS 5 model](https://www.nvidia.com/en-us/geforce/news/dlss-5-faster-ai-model-hogwarts-legacy-rtx-spark-laptops/) will debut in [_NBA 2K27_](https://blogs.nvidia.com/blog/geforce-now-thursday-september-2026-games-list/?utm_source=chatgpt.com) on Oct. 16 on GeForce NOW, GeForce RTX 50 Series GPUs and RTX Spark laptops.

Dates listed above reflect when games are released on their respective stores. GeForce NOW availability may vary, as games are onboarded after they’re released and added throughout the week. Keep an eye on GeForce NOW channels and GFN Thursdays for availability updates to announced titles.

Gamers who want to test out the new 4.5 controls and high-performance GeForce NOW cloud gaming can start with a [day pass](https://www.nvidia.com/en-us/geforce-now/?ncid=pa-srch-goog-673352&gad_source=1&gad_campaignid=24109411186&gbraid=0AAAAAD4XAoGPVGKakiCteqkRtoF1Q-KSI&gclid=CjwKCAjws_DTBhB_EiwAXZknGUBjXpM5vNQvnwLXUGilFsIHBSkbKPfllg7RGpFFuQZv2GFityJC6BoCq8MQAvD_BwE) to try premium cloud gaming before committing to a membership. Better yet, the cost of the day pass can be applied toward a first monthly membership — making it easy to try GeForce RTX-powered cloud gaming with the latest releases, then level up for more.

What’s on the playlist this weekend? Let us know on [X](https://x.com/NVIDIAGFN?lang=en) or in the comments below.

Title: NVIDIA Expands Advanced Technology Access for Europe’s Scientific Community Through Open Learning Resources, Collaborations and Compute

URL Source: https://blogs.nvidia.com/blog/ec-scientific-computing-pledge/

Published Time: 2026-10-15T10:00:12+00:00

Markdown Content:
Much of today’s scientific progress begins with computation.

But turning accelerated computing’s potential into scientific progress — modeling climate systems, designing molecules, simulating materials and more — depends on more than breakthrough technology. Especially for smaller labs, early-career scientists or science-based startups, the hardest part of research can be everything that comes before the science: assembling tools, finding compute and building the expertise to use both.

At the AI in Science Summit in Dublin today, the European Commission launched the AI in Science Enablers Initiative, a shared framework connected to RAISE — the Resource for AI Science in Europe — that brings private-sector support closer to Europe’s research community.

NVIDIA is [joining the campaign](https://research-and-innovation.ec.europa.eu/strategy/strategy-research-and-innovation/our-digital-future/european-ai-science-strategy_en), providing:

*   Access to accelerated tools, models and platforms
*   Compute, cloud resources, data and scientific resources
*   Skills, training and technical support
*   Collaborative projects and pilots along with support for researchers and talent
*   Support for startups and ecosystem development

“Europe’s ambition in AI in science can only become reality if we bring together the strengths of our research community, industry and other partners,” Ekaterina Zaharieva, European Commissioner for Startups, Research and Innovation. “Through the AI in Science Enablers campaign, we are turning this ambition into concrete commitments that give researchers access to the tools, expertise and resources they need to innovate.”

## **Open Models**

NVIDIA’s pledge begins with open source technology.

NVIDIA has released more than 250 open models, 250 open datasets and over 1,400 open source software projects spanning large language models, healthcare, robotics, climate science, physical AI, autonomous vehicles and scientific research. The models and datasets are available on Hugging Face and GitHub.

Building on this open ecosystem, researchers can build agentic reasoning capabilities with [NVIDIA Nemotron](https://www.nvidia.com/en-us/ai-data-science/foundation-models/nemotron/) — a family of architectures, open weights, open source models, training data and recipes — and scientific software including [NVIDIA BioNeMo Agent Toolkit](https://nvidianews.nvidia.com/news/nvidia-launches-bionemo-agent-toolkit-giving-ai-agents-the-tools-to-accelerate-scientific-discovery), [NVIDIA PhysicsNeMo](https://developer.nvidia.com/physicsnemo) libraries, [NVIDIA Earth-2](https://www.nvidia.com/en-us/high-performance-computing/earth-2/) models and [NVIDIA ALCHEMI NIM microservices](https://developer.nvidia.com/cuda/cuda-x-libraries/alchemi) to accelerate research across biology, chemistry, molecular design, weather and climate, energy, engineering, physics and material sciences.

## **Skills and Training**

Building advanced intelligence capability across Europe requires knowledge that travels as freely as compute.

The NVIDIA Deep Learning Institute has launched a new[open source courseware hub](https://www.nvidia.com/en-eu/training/open-source/) with hands-on course materials covering accelerated computing and deep learning — freely downloadable and openly licensed, with no enrollment, fees or deadline.

Modular by design, the courses can be adapted for university curricula, supercomputing center bootcamps or developer community events, and serve as a direct bridge to NVIDIA’s broader[training and certification programs](https://www.nvidia.com/en-eu/training/).

NVIDIA is collaborating with cloud infrastructure partners and European national AI factories — including in [France](https://blogs.nvidia.com/blog/france-ecosystem-agentic-computing), Spain and [Sweden](https://blogs.nvidia.com/blog/nordics-technology-ecosystem)— to open new routes for startups and small- and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs) to access sovereign European compute and services.

The [NVIDIA Inception](https://www.nvidia.com/en-eu/startups/) program for startups provides access to compute resources and technical support, lowering the barrier to entry for startups seeking high-performance infrastructure and technological education.

AI2F in France is the first AI factory to have collaborated with the Inception program for four months, demonstrating strong results.

The BSC AI Factory ran a pilot initiative and is now rolling out its first full accelerator program, with growing interest from other European national AI factories in replicating the model in 2027. Beyond startup support, this program is designed to contribute to a broader strategic objective: building self-sustaining AI ventures in Spain and Europe.

[Sweden AI Factory](https://www.ri.se/en/news/sweden-ai-factory-and-nvidia-collaborate-to-shape-the-future-of-swedish-ai), one of Europe’s 19 EuroHPC-funded AI factories, announced a collaboration with NVIDIA to open its infrastructure and expertise to Inception startups and SMEs enterprises across sectors including life and material sciences, autonomous systems and gaming.

Finally, EuroHPC supercomputing centers such as CINECA and JSC provide academia and startups with free access to NVIDIA GPU infrastructure and services for open research. NVIDIA complements this access with office hours, bootcamps and hackathons that help researchers fine-tune models on their own datasets.

As an example, NVIDIA is co-organizing an European AI hackathon this month alongside Austrian Scientific Computing, the Leibniz Supercomputing Centre, the High-Performance Computing Center Stuttgart and The Cyprus Institute, for Pharos-CY.

## **AI Infrastructure Expansion**

To top it all off, NVIDIA is powering Europe’s most ambitious expansion of AI infrastructure to date, with [35 supercomputers](https://nvidianews.nvidia.com/news/europe-unveils-a-record-35-new-nvidia-ai-supercomputers) currently in development across the continent — the largest single-year buildout of supercomputing capacity Europe has ever seen.

Together, these systems will equip [over 3 million researchers](https://nvidianews.nvidia.com/news/europe-unveils-a-record-35-new-nvidia-ai-supercomputers) with next-generation infrastructure, accelerating discovery across domains from climate science and drug development to materials research and beyond.

_Explore_[_NVIDIA technologies for science_](https://www.nvidia.com/en-us/high-performance-computing/hpc-and-ai/)_and_[_open source courseware_](https://www.nvidia.com/en-eu/training/open-source/)_, and find hands-on training through the_[_NVIDIA Deep Learning Institute_](https://www.nvidia.com/en-eu/training/)_._

_Follow the European Commission’s_[_RAISE Pledging Initiative_](https://research-and-innovation.ec.europa.eu/strategy/strategy-research-and-innovation/our-digital-future/european-ai-science-strategy/raise-resource-ai-science-europe/raise-pledging-initiative-ai-science-enablers_en)_._

Title: The Nordics and NVIDIA Show What’s Possible When a Region Commits to Advanced Computing

URL Source: https://blogs.nvidia.com/blog/nordics-technology-ecosystem/

Published Time: 2026-10-15T05:00:12+00:00

Markdown Content:
The Nordic countries have become the European leader in unicorn startup density, producing the most emerging companies valued at $1 billion or more per capita on the continent.

Now, a new chapter for the region is unfolding as countries race to build one of Europe’s most consequential technology ecosystems.

The many computing advancements already underway in the Nordics, combined with the opportunity that lies ahead, signal a region moving from ambition to application.

## **NVIDIA’s Investments in the Nordics**

Over the past year, NVIDIA has invested in the technology ecosystem in the Nordics, including Sweden’s leading startups Lovable and Legora.

Lovable, a Stockholm-based startup, provides a software creation platform that enables anyone to build and run software using plain language. In collaboration with NVIDIA, Lovable is optimizing inference for open models and training its models using NVIDIA Dynamo software and Nemotron tools.

Legora provides an agentic operating system for legal work, supporting lawyers in research, review and drafting across complex matters.

## **Nordics Emerge as Infrastructure Hub**

The foundation for establishing the Nordics as a technology powerhouse is already being built and the region holds a structural advantage: abundant renewable energy, rigorous data governance and a research tradition that bridges academia and industry.

The Nordics are one of Europe’s fastest growing hubs for infrastructure. AI clouds are expanding with a projected 1 gigawatts of capacity to be deployed across the region by the end of 2027. Among these cloud providers are Bitdeer,CoreWeave, Crusoe, Hyperstack,Nscale, Verda and Volta.

In Sweden, a consortium anchored by Ericsson, AstraZeneca, Saab, SEB and Wallenberg Investments, with SKF as strategic partner, launched [Sferical One](https://sferical.ai/newsroom/leading-swedish-companies-launch-sferical-one-shared-ai-supercomputer) — a shared supercomputer running on two [NVIDIA DGX SuperPODs](https://www.nvidia.com/en-us/data-center/dgx-superpod/) with 16 racks of [NVIDIA DGX GB300 systems](https://www.nvidia.com/en-us/data-center/dgx-gb300/) and 1,152 GPUs. The consortium will build services using [NVIDIA Nemotron](https://www.nvidia.com/en-us/ai-data-science/foundation-models/nemotron/) open models, which allow researchers to customize and deploy their models in a secure environment.

## **Nordic-Built Intelligence**

Some of the Nordics’ leading technology companies are now building proprietary intelligence on NVIDIA infrastructure.

Spotify, which personalizes music, podcasts and audiobooks for hundreds of millions of listeners, uses NVIDIA TensorRT-LLM inference software to run AI-powered podcast recommendations faster and cheaper at scale. The deployment is a case study in inference efficiency: delivering the same recommendations to a global audience at a lower cost per query.

[ABB Robotics](https://www.abb.com/global/en/news/137409/abb-robotics-and-nvidia-white-paper-defines-transformative-impact-of-physical-ai-on-manufacturing) developed RobotStudio HyperReality using [NVIDIA Omniverse](https://www.nvidia.com/en-us/omniverse/) libraries to bridge the gap between robot simulations and real-world performance. By combining NVIDIA’s advanced simulation capabilities with ABB Robotics’ virtual controller, running the same firmware as its physical robots, the solution enables engineers to train, test and validate robots virtually, while using real-world data to continuously improve the digital model. According to ABB Robotics, the solution delivers up to 99% simulation accuracy and reduces commissioning time by up to 80%.

Finnish telecom company [Elisa](https://nam11.safelinks.protection.outlook.com/?url=https%3A%2F%2Fyrityksille.elisa.fi%2Fideat%2Fmoontalk-airi-real-time-ai-assistance&data=05%7C02%7Cebeisswenger%40nvidia.com%7Ce4430ec4c92b4ed0c2d508df29bf8858%7C43083d15727340c1b7db39efd9ccc17a%7C0%7C0%7C639275574771855820%7CUnknown%7CTWFpbGZsb3d8eyJFbXB0eU1hcGkiOnRydWUsIlYiOiIwLjAuMDAwMCIsIlAiOiJXaW4zMiIsIkFOIjoiTWFpbCIsIldUIjoyfQ%3D%3D%7C0%7C%7C%7C&sdata=%2Bv8nQ8VMmNnfXQBVAQfHXnCS8ch%2B68zVKKfA8xo6wq0%3D&reserved=0) is launching a beta of Moontalk AIRI, a real-time enterprise agentic assistant that retrieves information, captures insights and documents decisions during meetings and calls. Built on NVIDIA Nemotron open models and distributed infrastructure, it uses company data and low-latency networking to deliver fast, context-aware responses.

## **Nordic Startups Scaling on NVIDIA**

Sweden’s startup ecosystem raised $2.8 billion in the first half of 2026 and is projected to reach $5 billion for the year. This next generation is building fast — and on open models.

[Stilta](https://stilta.com/news/stilta-nvidia-partnership) is reinventing how companies protect their inventions with intellectual property. The Stockholm-based startup is post-training NVIDIA Nemotron open models to scale patent analysis from a single patent to entire portfolios — work that was previously out of reach. Nemotron gives Stilta the language model accuracy for continuous portfolio monitoring at scale, across the thousands of patents that large industrial and technology companies hold.

[ConfidentialMind’s SampoTron](https://confidentialmind.com/blog/sampotron-adapting-queries-reusing-index), built on NVIDIA Nemotron-3-Embed, delivers more than 20% improvement in cross-lingual retrieval accuracy across English, Finnish and Swedish.

[Agaton](https://www.agaton.ai/post/nvidia-nemotron), a platform that analyzes customer conversations in real time, is using NVIDIA Nemotron 3.5 Lightning to speed up Revenue Mining solution on live sales calls. By routing knowledge retrieval to Nemotron 3.5 Lightning, Agaton can cut response latency to deliver fast responses that inform customers’ buying decisions.

[Klang](https://research.klang.ai/releases/pianissimo/), a Swedish speech lab, fine-tuned the NVIDIA Parakeet v3 model to create Pianissimo — a Swedish transcription model that reduces errors by 75% while being 64x faster than the most accurate alternative. Built on over 50,000 hours of Swedish speech using the open source [NVIDIA NeMo](https://www.nvidia.com/en-us/ai-data-science/products/nemo/) framework, the model is freely available on Hugging Face.

[Embedl](https://embedl.com/news/embedl-and-space-cargo-unlimited-bring-ai-autonomy-to-the-space-edge), founded in Gothenburg and a member of the [NVIDIA Inception](https://www.nvidia.com/en-us/startups/) program for cutting-edge startups, and Space Cargo Unlimited unveiled an onboard prototype that monitors protein crystallization, flags anomalies and recommends actions on a single NVIDIA Jetson Orin NX module, without continuous ground connectivity.

[Sweden AI Factory](https://www.ri.se/en/news/sweden-ai-factory-and-nvidia-collaborate-to-shape-the-future-of-swedish-ai) — one of Europe’s 19 EuroHPC-funded AI factories — announced a collaboration with NVIDIA to open its infrastructure and expertise to Inception startups and small- and medium-sized enterprises across industries, including life and material sciences, autonomous systems and gaming.

## **Autonomous Machines on Nordic Roads and Factory Floors**

In Sweden, advanced computing is also powering vehicles on the road and machines in factories.

[Volvo Cars](https://nvidianews.nvidia.com/news/volvo-cars-and-nvidia-expand-partnership-to-advance-safe-automated-driving) is combining its industry-leading vehicle safety systems and engineering expertise with [NVIDIA Hyperion](https://www.nvidia.com/en-us/solutions/autonomous-vehicles/), Halos OS and Alpamayo Stack to enable future Volvo cars to safely navigate complex real-world environments from door to door.

Autonomous freight company[Einride](https://www.einride.tech/press/3365322)is building its next-generation Einride Driver on NVIDIA Hyperion for autonomous freight trucks, using the [NVIDIA Halos](https://www.nvidia.com/en-us/ai-trust-center/halos/autonomous-vehicles/) safety system and [NVIDIA Cosmos](https://www.nvidia.com/en-us/ai/cosmos/) open world models.

Meanwhile, [Toyota Material Handling Europe](https://toyota-forklifts.eu/about-toyota/news-and-editorials/toyota-material-handling-europe-and-softserve-to-reduce-autonomous-solution-commissioning-time-by-50-percent-using-nvidia-physical-ai/)— the world’s leading forklift manufacturer — is bringing autonomous machines to factory floors. In a collaboration with NVIDIA and SoftServe,Toyota Material Handling Europe is adopting a simulation-first approach to autonomous material handling, cutting autonomous solution deployment time by up to 50% across its global engineering, manufacturing and innovation teams.

[Norrsken Foundation](https://www.norrsken.org/houses/stockholm-ai-lab) and NVIDIA are opening the Stockholm AI Lab, a physical hub for AI-native founders working on global challenges, set to open in 2027.

## **Quantum Meets Accelerated Computing**

Finally, Swedish companies are advancing quantum research using NVIDIA’s quantum computing platform.

Stockholm-based[FirstQFM](https://firstqfm.com/news/firstqfm-nvidia-gtc-2026) used NVIDIA accelerated computing to train a model that reduces the execution time of quantum processors by 33% without sacrificing performance. Validated on a QuantWare quantum processor unit, this model optimizes how the operations needed by quantum algorithms are turned into detailed hardware instructions, accounting for detailed updates on how the hardware is calibrated.

Zach Yadegari has enjoyed an immense amount of success for someone who only recently graduated from high school. Founder of the AI-fueled calorie tracking app Cal AI, Yadegari is only 19, but his company has rocketed to viral fame over the past two years. At TechCrunch Disrupt on Thursday, Yadegari shared details of that surprising rise to prominence.
Cal AI, which was founded in 2024, exploded its presence on the internet thanks largely to Yadegari’s strategy of deploying a small army of influencers to promote the brand. The company generated over $30 million in revenue in two years and was
acquired by MyFitness
for an undisclosed amount of money in March.
Discussing his social strategy onstage, Yadegari noted that an early sign of success came when an influencer’s post about them led to approximately a thousand new users over the course of two days.
“From there, we figured out, okay, this can actually work for us, and so we started recruiting influencers as fast as we could — paying as many people as possible to start posting for us,” he said. “What we saw was that it was a clear formula. It was pretty linear, but it was extremely fast. I guess linear in the sense that every post they did would get a certain number of viewers that would convert.”
The Forbes 30 Under 30 alumnus told the audience that part of his company’s strategy was to negotiate rates with influencers, promising them certain payouts for a certain scale of reach. A lot of influencers are “broke college kids” who are “just want cash,” Yadegari added. “You just ask them, okay, we’ll pay you this, but we need to get us at least this amount of use and keep posting until you get there.”
Another important component of success was finding the right influencers whose reach can be quantified. “The biggest thing for us was finding influencers that had very tight communities,” the founder said.
Yadegari, whose father was in the audience, also credited his family with giving him the freedom to go after his ambitions. Does he also credit higher education for his success? Not so much.
“I think the only real reason to go to college is if you want to have a fun social time as a kid and be with other people,” he said, to audience laughter.
Earlier this month, Yadegari also launched Persona, a new AI agent startup that
has already raised $10 million
.
Yadegari said the “overarching mission” with Persona is to “make computing seamless with human life.” The company’s personal AI assistant will “live anyplace with internet connection,” he said, including “iMessage, app, email, phone call.” He added that part of what distinguishes the company’s plans for this AI assistant is to build a “hardware ecosystem around” the app.

Meta has
launched
what it calls the “most capable” open-weight model in the United States. Dubbed Muse Spark Open, the model also has the distinction of having been designed to work with Macs.
The new model, which leverages 816 billion parameters and a 1 million token context window, claims to offer superior performance to other popular open-weight models, according to evaluation results released by Meta on Thursday.
Muse Spark Open is natively multimodal and built for complex coding tasks and agentic labor. It has also been designed to run locally on Apple’s computers. However, you will still need a lot of power to run the model locally, with a requirement of at least 1 terabyte of RAM,
per Engadget
. The model will run best via the Mac Studio that comes equipped with the M5 Ultra chip.
Still, if you can muster the memory, Muse Spark Open may prove a significant work horse for coding and other desktop tasks. Meta says that it paired the model with Muse Code, its AI coding terminal, and deployed it to various agentic workflows, including coding fixes for a Mastodon client that included “bug fixes, new features, [and] full build.”
The company says it also deployed it in the service of running DaVinci Resolve, the high-end video editing software, revealing that the model was capable of reviewing and cropping footage.
Open-weight models provide a number of distinct industry advantages that aren’t afforded by closed and proprietary models. Open-weight models can be significantly more cost-efficient and can also offer transparency and flexibility that closed source models don’t allow.
Meta is making the new model available now through a number of different API platforms.

Amazon is placing its bets on ambient computing, not apps, as the future of personal AI.
Alongside the
launch of the company’s new AI wearables from Bee
, Panos Panay, who serves as Amazon’s SVP of Devices, Alexa & Leo, took the stage at
TechCrunch Disrupt
on Thursday to talk more in depth about where he sees personal computing headed.
“A lot of times, what you’re doing right now — what we all do right now — is we have to remember what we’re asking our tool to do for us,” Panay began, explaining that this is how we engage with our modern smartphones. “It’s like point, shoot, return,” Panay continued. “I think where we’re headed is a world [that] starts with ambient devices.”
By “ambient devices,” he means those that work quietly in the background, using sensors and AI to help you figure out what needs to be done, instead of the other way around, where you’re telling the device what you need to do.
“As it works in the background, you’re able to stay more present. You’re able to get more done. You’re about to spend more time with people … you’re not afraid if you miss something. It’s incredibly powerful,” Panay said.
Amazon’s biggest entry into this space is the set of new Bee devices it introduced on Thursday, which include a band you can wear on your wrist or detach to wear as a pendant, as well as a new credit-card-sized device that attaches magnetically to the back of your smartphone.
These gadgets passively record audio and take notes about your day, finding the to-dos, reminders, and insights you may later need to refer back to. To balance the need to be useful with user privacy, Bee’s devices don’t actually store the raw audio from your conversations; they process the audio in real time and then delete it when done. Transcripts of conversations are encrypted using keys that your device creates and controls. That means no one else, including Amazon employees, can access those files unless you intentionally share them.
Panay said that privacy was a key consideration for how these new ambient devices should work.
“You have to give customers that control,” he said. “Every product is different, but for Bee specifically, as an example in the ambient space like that, you have to design with privacy in mind. And that’s what we do. That’s critical.”
The executive, who came to Amazon after 19 years at Microsoft where he oversaw the development of Surface devices, has spent a lot of his life thinking about how personal computing will evolve. With Bee — and ambient computing more generally — Panay also envisioned a future where the idea of interacting with apps becomes less important, as more tasks are handled via AI.
“Do I think we have a future where there’s a bit of a balance — a whole generation that doesn’t say ‘give me the app’ for that, but says it should just understand what I need? Yeah, I do. I think that transformation is coming. I think that is the next generation,” he said.
That doesn’t necessarily mean the smartphone itself won’t continue to be an important personal computing device (as much as Amazon would like it to be an Alexa tablet or Echo smart speaker), Panay pointed out. Rather, he believes a new crop of devices will emerge that use sensors to understand users better, and to bring intelligence to the world around you.
“I’m not a proponent that says one form factor is going to replace another. I don’t think that’s the case,” he clarified. “I think there’s an intelligence layer that connects it all … and it has to be useful.”

articles.content:
Anthropic is giving employee-level access to six researchers from
METR
, a nonprofit that tests frontier AI models, to independently assess Anthropic’s models, safety practices, and risk management, the company said in a
blog post
on Thursday.
The arrangement comes at a time where incidents of AI agents acting outside their instructions have been
disclosed
every
week
or
two
since late August. The incidents have sharpened calls for independent checks on AI companies.
“We want to be publicly accountable for the decisions we’re making,” Anthropic said in the blog post. “We aim to close the gap between what evaluators understand about a frontier AI company’s systems and what the company itself understands.”
Under the new arrangement, the METR team has Anthropic-issued company laptops, office space, and access to internal tools roughly on par with what Anthropic’s own risk assessment teams use. “Anthropic employees are encouraged to share information with them just as they would with a fellow employee working on alignment risk” the company said.
Anthropic compared the arrangement to banking, similar to how regulators place resident examiners inside the largest banks.
METR will publish its own assessments of Anthropic’s risks, incidents, and practices, and the company has given up the right to block them.
“Anthropic can’t veto publication, but we can require them to redact information if it falls into narrow, pre-defined categories,” the company said, such as customer data, anything attorney-client privileged, or relating to information about its model architectures. “METR is free to characterize our redactions publicly, and say whether it believes the redactions were justified, as long as it does so without revealing the redacted information” Anthropic added.
METR is the only evaluator so far at the top of a three-tier system Anthropic is building. Evaluators in the bottom tier, like biosecurity nonprofit SecureBio, run narrow reviews and require Anthropic’s approval to publish. The middle tier gets more information and can publish without approval, while the top tier adds METR’s employee-level access.
Thursday’s announcement makes good on a promise Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei made
in a September essay
, where he proposed embedding outside evaluators inside AI labs as a first step toward slowing the technology’s development.
OpenAI quickly pledged the same
, and both companies, along with Google, Meta, Nvidia, and xAI, have since signed a White House accord committing to independent review.

articles.content:
Open social network Bluesky is once again expanding beyond its flagship app. At
TechCrunch Disrupt 2026
on Thursday, the company announced the launch of a new tool that allows creators to make websites, quizzes, games, polls, and other interactive experiences.
The tool is an expansion of
Attie, Bluesky’s more experimental platform
, which initially offered AI-powered technology for building custom social feeds. With its new creation capabilities, the idea is to allow everyday users to create the kind of experiences that previously only software developers could build.
These user-created games, sites, and other experiences will also live on the same AT Protocol (ATProto) that powers Bluesky and other decentralized social apps that make up the decentralized social web known as the Atmosphere.
Bluesky CEO Toni Schneider shared the news of Attie’s new capabilities during an interview at Disrupt, saying, “We’re adding a feature to our Attie product that allows you to build sites and social experiences again for a group of people. So think of it as … social vibe coding or vibe coding for your community.”
The exec, a former CEO of Automattic and a partner at True Ventures, had previously been leading the company on an interim basis after former CEO Jay Graber
stepped down
in March to become Bluesky’s chief innovation officer. Now he’s taking charge of the company as it enters the AI era.
Attie offers Bluesky a playground where it can try out AI-powered ideas like this.
Image Credits:
Bluesky
“Vibe coding today is kind of a single-user, solo experience,” Schneider explained. “And what I want to be able to do is build together or build for a group of people, and that’s what this product does.”
When creators build with Attie, they’re connected to their ATProto identity. Plus, Attie will suggest things users might want to make based on their public Bluesky profiles.
To build with Attie, users can bring their own AI model or use open-weight options, and the resulting sites and games can then tap into Bluesky’s wider audience, noted Bluesky COO Rose Wang.
“Everybody is building … But the big question is: Who’s using the thing you’re building, because we haven’t solved that problem with distribution,” she said. “What makes Attie so interesting is that it comes with the Bluesky distribution, so it doesn’t stand alone.”
That network today has
47 million registered users
, though it’s seen
a decline in engagement
, as some users who tested it out later returned to X.
Beyond being a testing ground for new ideas, Attie ties into Bluesky’s larger plans to reinvigorate activity on its network by focusing on both developers and communities in the months ahead. Those areas will also be supercharged by the protocol’s forthcoming support for private data, which Schneider said has been the biggest request from developers. Private data is now in alpha testing, with plans for a rollout by the end of the year, he said.
“There should be lots and lots of these fun, small social experiences for your friends,” said Schneider, referencing the types of projects Attie will enable. “We don’t all have to go communicate with the entire world all the time.”

articles.content:
Rivian recently rolled out an AI assistant that lets drivers and passengers interact with the company’s electric vehicles just by talking to them. But the carmaker’s founder and CEO, RJ Scaringe, said at TechCrunch Disrupt this week that, in the future, Rivian’s cars will be able to run AI agents made by other companies like Anthropic.
“That’s where it becomes magical,” Scaringe said onstage.
Scaringe didn’t say when Rivian would implement this, and the company declined to offer more details, pointing instead to the “AI & Autonomy Day” event it’s hosting in December.
But it’s not hard to imagine how Rivian might integrate something like Claude, OpenAI’s Dots, or Meta’s Muse assistant into its software. The company has developed its in-car software from the ground up, instead of leaning on Apple CarPlay or Android Auto, and built a lot of its own applications, like navigation (though it has worked to integrate popular in-car apps like Apple Music).
Rivian says it has created its own in-house agentic framework that understands what action a person wants to take when they talk to the vehicle, and routes it to the right part of the car’s software. Most of the time, that involves what you’d expect: asking the car to turn down the temperature, activate the seat warmers, or summarize the news.
“Think of it as like a traffic light. So if you ask the vehicle something, it decides what model it’s going to use. It can use a local model that’s running on the edge and the vehicle. If it’s a more complex question, it can go up to the cloud. And then even for that, we have different models that we use,” Scaringe said.
As of May of this year, the agent could access external apps like Google Calendar. And Scaringe said at Disrupt the next step would be to add products from the frontier AI companies, though making them work in the car won’t be easy.
“There’s a lot of plumbing behind the scenes we have to do to make sure that that works, and it’s not just within Rivian. That’s also a lot of coordination with the labs to make sure they enable that plumbing,” he said, adding that putting this kind of software near safety-critical systems means Rivian has to be extremely careful.
“You wouldn’t want an agent to determine, ‘hey, it’s time to apply the brakes, or time to steer the vehicle.’ So anything that’s vehicle-level controls are not being handed to an agent,” he said.
Instead, he thinks the implementation will look more like an extension of how people currently use these agentic apps. That would mean Rivian would have to find a way to connect the vehicle to all of the context that apps like Muse collect on their users.
For example, Scaringe said, a driver could ask the Rivian assistant to turn on the ventilated seats before going deeper. “And then simultaneously say, ‘We were talking yesterday about this meal. I’m planning to have guests over on Friday. Can you help me think through what we’re going to make?’,” he said. The car could then pull the driver’s context from a conversation they had with the assistant on another device.
Of course, Rivian wouldn’t be the first American car company to add AI agents to a car’s software. Earlier this year, Tesla added a feature that let users talk to both SpaceX’s Grok chatbot and also its Grok Bot assistant.

articles.content:
Google on Thursday
said
“Universal Cart,” a tool that lets users collect and monitor products they find across search and in the Gemini app, is now available to U.S. users. The company first
previewed the tool
at Google I/O in May.
The idea is to make online shopping easier to manage. Find something you like, save it to your cart, and move on. When you return later, your items and shopping progress are still there, so you don’t have to hunt down the same products or start over. Universal Cart can collect items from multiple retailers, turning it into a central hub for browsing and keeping track of potential purchases.
Google says the cart can also help shoppers stay on top of deals and availability. The tool can send notifications when a saved product’s price drops or when an out-of-stock item becomes available again.
The tool is also designed to offer more tailored help during the shopping process. Google says it can take credit card perks into account when helping users choose how to pay, and also surface relevant promo codes.
Checkout is tied to Google’s Universal Commerce Protocol, or UCP, an open standard the company introduced earlier this year. UCP is designed to help AI agents and retailers work together across different parts of the shopping journey, including checkout.
Google is already deeply invested in AI-powered shopping, and Universal Cart is its latest effort to make the experience more convenient. It joins features such as conversational product discovery in Search’s AI Mode and Google’s
“Let Google Call”
tool, which uses an AI agent to contact nearby stores and check whether an item is in stock.
Google isn’t the only company bringing AI into e-commerce.
Amazon
,
OpenAI
, and other rivals have added agentic commerce features as companies look for ways to make chatbots useful beyond answering questions.

Amazon’s personal AI wearable maker,
Bee
, is announcing its first new products since being
acquired by the retail giant last year
. The tech company on Thursday introduced the Bee Frontier, the next generation of its device that can be worn on the wrist or pinned to clothes, along with Bee Eclipse, a credit-card-sized device that magnetically attaches to the back of your smartphone.
The latter puts Bee into more direct competition with AI devices like the Plaud Note or Pocket, but at a lower price point — the Bee Frontier is $74.99, compared with $159 for the
Plaud Note
(or $189 for the Note Pro), or $129 for the
Pocket AI device
.
The Bee Frontier will come in Onyx, Lavender, and Sage, while the $99.99 Bee Eclipse will be offered in Silver, Midnight, Honey, and Blush.
Image Credits:
Amazon
Like the original Bee, the idea with the new devices is to leverage AI to take notes from your everyday conversations, allowing you to remember the important things that were said, and then turn those into actionable to-dos, summaries, and insights.
For instance, if you discussed making plans with friends, the Bee would remember the date and time you agreed on, then create a calendar invite. You could also use the Bee to take lecture notes in class, or to jot down the care plan you discussed with a doctor, among other things.
Image Credits:
Amazon
All Bee devices can create conversation summaries and recaps for free, and offer 14 days of memory. With an $11.99 per month Bee Pro subscription, users receive unlimited conversation summaries and integrations with Amazon.com, Alexa+, and third-party applications. Pro users also get suggested to-dos, daily memories, a personal chat assistant, and conversation templates.
To make all this possible, Bee devices use a private computing security architecture, which doesn’t store the raw audio from your conversations. Instead, audio is processed in real time and then deleted. Transcripts of the conversation are encrypted using keys that your device creates and controls, which means no one else, including Amazon employees, can access those files unless you manually and intentionally share them.
In addition, you can opt to connect the Bee to Alexa, allowing your Echo device to use its ability to identify your voice, a feature called Voice ID, to recognize when you’re speaking. It can then record your conversations to provide Bee’s insights. (This aspect of Bee is optional, and Amazon notes you can delete transcripts and summaries at any time.)
With its new connections to Amazon.com and Alexa, Bee users can make purchases from Amazon or ask Alexa for their Bee insights, summaries, or to-dos hands-free.
Bee also works with your existing productivity software, like Gmail, Google Calendar, and Microsoft Outlook, so it can draft emails, set up meetings, surface action items, and more.
Plus, you can upload photos to Bee or connect it with Apple’s HealthKit to add a picture of your overall wellness to be integrated into your provided insights.
The Bee Frontier and Bee Eclipse both have just one button that turns the device off and on, and include an indicator light when it’s summarizing a conversation. The Frontier also offers IP67 water resistance, up to seven days of battery life, USB-C charging, and dual microphones with advanced noise filtering.
All Bee devices come with a companion mobile app, which has also been newly redesigned, plus a new desktop app.
The Bee Frontier is available now on Amazon, and the Eclipse will be available soon thereafter.

Design platform Figma announced a new Markdown-based editor to help define a company’s design, bring in design and code libraries, and integrate with the Payload headless content management system during the company’s first Config event in India. Through some of these features, the company aims to provide a definition for its own and third-party agents to adhere to a brand’s design rules better while creating with AI.
The company debuted a new feature called Figma Specs, which is a markdown editor that lets users define their design language in a simple way. The document can serve as a reference for teams and agents while designing in Figma. Specs can exist as a standalone file in Figma or can co-exist within the canvas. Apart from acting as a text editor, users can reference other Figma elements, such as elements on the canvas, and embed FigJam diagrams, code layers, and designs.
What’s more, teams can bring in more context about design, including design libraries, code libraries, and guidelines to manage context for the design system. Agents can also refer to this centralized system to adhere to rules.
Image Credits:
Figma
In the past week, the company made its agent on canvas available to a wider user base. However, given the non-deterministic nature of AI, the company is providing tools to steer it toward more predictable outcomes.
Figma also made its code layers feature available to users in open beta, which adds coding to designs on canvas for more interactive prototypes. The company
announced this feature
in private beta back in June. At its India event this week, the company is making the function available in public beta to let more users test it out. Users can also ask the agent to turn a design into code or change a part of the code to iterate on a prototype.
Image Credits:
Figma
“We see Figma as the place where software teams come to decide what they build and ship. And so for that, I think one of the key things to keep in mind about what AI has changed and what it made available is the ability to build,” Figma’s chief design officer Loredana Crisan told TechCrunch. “There are 17-times more lines of code being produced today than in the past. But when you’re looking at releases, only 1.3-times more releases. A lot of that code actually is not necessarily built to ship, but really built to discover what the product is. It’s built to design.”
The company said it is also supporting over 20 new tools with its MCP, including Open Code, Dia, Grok Bot, and Indian AI startup Sarvam.
Last year, Figma acquired
open source headless CMS Payload
. Now, the company is integrating it with its Figma Make product for generating dynamic websites and directly managing content. The company said that Payload’s downloads have increased sixfold in the last 12 months.
The company opened its
first office in India late last year with sales
, partnership, go-to-market, and product support functions. Figma said that the country is its biggest market in terms of users outside the United States. The company noted that the platform works with 40% of India’s top 100 companies listed on the Bombay Stock Exchange.

articles.content:
Ricursive Intelligence
founders Anna Goldie and Azalia Mirhoseini believe more efficient AI chip design could help solve the compute crisis. The founders took the stage at TechCrunch Disrupt on Wednesday to detail how their
startup
is developing AI that can design chips, learn from each iteration, and improve subsequent designs, all with the goal of automating and accelerating the chip design process.
“There is this understanding that in the next five years we are going to have at least 10,000x more demand for compute, and that’s somewhat potentially conservative,” Goldie said on stage. “So we don’t want to build 10,000 times more data centers. We think that we need to help by making chips that are more efficient, that use the bandwidth in those data centers more efficiently, that use the wafers and fabs more efficiently, because even if we make [data centers] in space or something, I don’t know, you won’t see the sun anymore.”
While some may be scared by the thought of AI designing its own chips, Goldie argues that letting AI handle chip design will allow humans to focus on developing applications and exploring new possibilities that can expand what they can accomplish with computing.
Image Credits:
Kimberly White/Getty Images for TechCrunch
“I think the way everything is shifting is that humans bring their great ideas and creative thoughts, and execution is handled by AI,” Goldie said. “And this is happening in chip design, software development, and other places. And that’s something that recursive does for chip design.”
The founders say AI is challenging traditional chip design methods by discovering unconventional layouts that can outperform traditional ones. For example, AlphaChip, the AI system the founders previously developed, produced a circular, “donut-shaped” arrangement of chip components that initially surprised engineers but ultimately proved to be successful.
They explained that they are optimizing entire chips rather than following the traditional approach of partitioning them into dozens of smaller blocks. This approach allows AI to create intricate patterns, including wave-like designs, which the pair said they plan to share more about in the future.
The founders also argued that AI-designed chips will make it possible to create all sorts of chips that might not have been possible before.
“If it takes six months or a year or two years to design a new chip, then you really have to be extremely selective about the chips that you design,” Goldie said. “But if you can design a chip in like a week, and then say for manufacturing, you can design custom chips for all sorts of different types of applications in like space and AR, VR, and biological computing, it makes sense financially to do that, and we can be more energy efficient.”
